sentences.text: Heard Mr. Das, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Dash, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
2. Instant I.As. are filed by the petitioner seeking stay realization of fine amount and release the petitioner on bail on the grounds stated therein.

3. It is submitted that the petitioner stands convicted for the offence under Section 376 read with Section 511 IPC and directed to undergo sentence of three years modified by the learned Court below while disposing of Criminal Appeal No.6 of 2017 for one year.
It is submitted that the petitioner was on bail during trial and pendency of the appeal and hence, he should be allowed to go on bail.
It is also submitted that the learned Trial Court issued NBWA against the petitioner upon disposal of Criminal Appeal No.6 of 2017 and the same is pending execution.
With such submission, release of the petitioner is requested for, whereas, a serious objection is received from Ms. Dash, the learned ASC for the State.
4. The circumstances leading to the lodging of FIR and the alleged mischief committed by the petitioner stand revealed from the impugned judgments at Annexures-1 & 2.
It was an attempt on the part of the petitioner to commit the mischief involving the victim.
The sentence awarded by the learned Trial Court stands reduced to one year as earlier stated by learned Court below.

Having regard to the above facts and the submission of the learned counsel for the respective parties with the claim that the petitioner was on bail during trial and at later stage, this Court is inclined to release him on bail with suitable conditions upon him surrendering before the Court of learned Assistant Sessions Judge Special Track Court, Rayagada in C.T. Case No.169 of 2016 taking into account I.A. No.547 of 2025, a copy of which is produced but not tagged with the record.
